forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.lead: Positive internal audit opinion provides assurance on control environment effectiveness; important context for interpreting specific audit findings and management remediation efforts.

news_drafts.lead: Multiple identified governance weaknesses indicate ongoing control environment development and emerging risks in LGR and cyber security areas.

findings.headline: Internal Audit opinion is positive: council operated effective framework of corporate governance, risk management and control
findings.detail: The Head of Mid Kent Audit provided a positive opinion on the overall adequacy and effectiveness of the council's framework of governance, risk management and control for 2025/26, rated as sound assurance. Work was completed with sufficient independence and in conformance with Global Internal Audit Standards.
findings.matters: Positive internal audit opinion provides assurance on control environment effectiveness; important context for interpreting specific audit findings and management remediation efforts.
findings.quote: A positive opinion had been given which was a sound assurance. The opinion states that, for the year 2025/26, the Council operated an effective framework of corporate governance, risk management and internal control.

findings.headline: Eight areas identified in Annual Governance Statement requiring governance improvement
findings.detail: The 2025/26 Annual Governance Statement identifies eight areas where improvements could be made, including arrangements for Local Government Reorganisation delivery, reviewing IT and Cyber Assessment Framework, and extending performance software to the Risk Register. Assurance ratings have been implemented to provide detail on council performance.
findings.matters: Multiple identified governance weaknesses indicate ongoing control environment development and emerging risks in LGR and cyber security areas.
findings.quote: There were eight areas where improvements could be made, which were contained within part 4 of the AGS, these included arrangements for the delivery of Local Government Reorganisation, reviewing the IT and Cyber Assessment Framework and building on the success of the Council's performance software development by extending it to the Risk Register.

findings.headline: External auditors propose £30,000 fee variation to cover work in respect of regaining assurance
findings.detail: Grant Thornton's external audit plan includes a proposed fee variation of £30,000 to cover additional work required to regain assurance. The audit plan identifies significant risks including management override of control, property and equipment, net pension fund liability and impairment risks on the Infinity Project.
findings.matters: Additional audit costs and expanded scope indicate prior audit concerns; lenders and peer councils need to understand why expanded audit procedures are necessary.
findings.quote: A proposed fee variation was proposed of £30,000 which would be determined by PSAA to cover the work in respect of regaining assurance.

findings.headline: HRA Housing Systems audit identified weak controls in Orchard/General Ledger Interface
findings.detail: Internal audit identified a weak audit finding in Housing Department systems, specifically the Orchard/General Ledger Interface. The draft report with findings has been accepted by management, and a final version is scheduled for presentation at the next Audit Committee meeting to commence the oversight process.
findings.matters: Weak controls in HRA accounting systems directly affect the reliability of HRA financial statements and cash management.
findings.quote: The Head of Mid Kent Audit reported on a weak audit in the Housing Department in respect of HRA Housing Systems, in particular the Orchard/General Ledger Interface – this had been issued in draft with the findings accepted.

findings.headline: Health and Safety control weakness remains outstanding: one recommendation from weak audit not yet completed
findings.detail: Following a weak audit of Health and Safety, significant progress has been made in governance, systems and operational delivery. However, one recommendation concerning risk assessment compliance remains outstanding. Risk assessment procedures have been refreshed and corporate oversight strengthened, but outstanding assessments across services are still being pursued. The Audit Committee requested a list of departments not providing risk assessments to be named at the next meeting.
findings.matters: Unresolved control findings from audit indicate incomplete remediation of material control weaknesses in a high-risk operational area.
findings.quote: One recommendation was outstanding – this was in relation to risk assessment compliance. Progress was underway with the risk assessment procedure having been refreshed and corporate oversight arrangements strengthened to improve consistency, assurance and the timely review of risk assessments across services.
